content.value_statement: Teams can lose important reasoning when decisions remain only in code or chat messages. This skill provides structured guidance for ADRs, API documentation, changelogs, and project conventions.
actual_capabilities: Explains when an Architecture Decision Record is appropriate.
Guides ADR structure, status, numbering, and repository placement.
Helps document public APIs with intent and usage context.
Provides guidance for README, changelog, and inline code documentation.
Encourages matching existing repository documentation conventions.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates, not automatic repository analysis.
It does not validate technical decisions or guarantee documentation accuracy.
It does not replace team review or stakeholder approval.
It does not generate diagrams, publish documentation, or run project commands.

use_cases.title: Record an architecture choice
use_cases.description: Create an ADR that explains a significant technical decision, its context, and its consequences.

use_cases.title: Document a public API change
use_cases.description: Add clear API documentation and release notes when a feature changes a public interface.

use_cases.title: Preserve project context
use_cases.description: Capture conventions and implementation reasoning so future contributors can work consistently.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me draft an ADR for choosing a database. Include context, decision, alternatives, consequences, and status.

prompt_templates.title: Document an API change
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me document this public API change. Explain the purpose, parameters, return values, migration steps, and compatibility impact.

prompt_templates.title: Align with repository conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing documentation conventions I provide. Then propose an ADR location, filename, numbering, and headings that match them.

prompt_templates.title: Plan documentation for a release
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a documentation plan for this release. Include ADR updates, API reference changes, README updates, changelog entries, owners, and review checks.

output_examples.input: Draft an ADR for adopting a message queue.
output: Title: Adopt a managed message queue
Context: Background jobs need reliable asynchronous processing.
Decision: Use a managed queue service with documented retry policies.
Consequences: Operations are simplified, but the service adds cost and vendor dependency.
API change: Rename createUser to registerUser.
Migration: Update callers to use registerUser before the next major release.
Changelog: Mark the old name as removed and link to the migration guide.

best_practices: Inspect existing project conventions before creating documentation.
Record the decision context and alternatives, not only the final choice.
Review documentation when public behavior or architecture changes.
anti_patterns: Do not create an ADR for a routine implementation detail.
Do not delete historical ADRs when a decision changes; mark them superseded.
Do not write comments that merely repeat what the code already states.

faq.question: What is an ADR?
faq.answer: An Architecture Decision Record explains an important technical decision, its context, and its consequences.

faq.question: When should I create an ADR?
faq.answer: Create one for decisions that affect architecture, public interfaces, security, operations, or long-term maintenance.

faq.question: Should I use the included ADR format exactly?
faq.answer: No. Follow the repository format when one already exists.

faq.question: Can this skill write API documentation?
faq.answer: It can guide clear API documentation with purpose, usage, behavior, and compatibility information.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands or modify files?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation guidance and contains no executable automation.

faq.question: How should old ADRs be handled?
faq.answer: Keep them as history and mark them superseded or deprecated when a newer decision replaces them.
